theme: Graphite GPU backend and new packages
highlights_headline: SkiaSharp 4.151.0 (unreleased) adds the Graphite GPU backend, async pixel reads, and a dedicated Vulkan/Silk.NET package.
highlights_body: The new Graphite bindings expose Vulkan, Metal, and Dawn GPU backends under the next-generation Skia renderer. An async `RequestReadPixels` API lands on SKImage and SKSurface, a new `SkiaSharp.Vulkan.Silk.NET` integration package ships, FreeType brings fonts to Nano Server, and several performance and memory fixes round out the release.

bullets.detail: Additional chrome/m151 upstream syncs harden the engine and keep the submodule current with the latest stability fixes.

bullets.lead: Graphite GPU backend bindings for Vulkan, Metal, and Dawn
bullets.detail: The new next-generation Skia Graphite renderer is now bound in SkiaSharp, exposing Vulkan, Metal, and Dawn backends alongside the existing Ganesh path.

bullets.lead: Async RequestReadPixels on SKImage and SKSurface
bullets.detail: A new backend-neutral `RequestReadPixels` API lets callers schedule an asynchronous pixel readback without blocking the rendering thread.
A new NuGet package wires SkiaSharp's Vulkan backend directly to the Silk.NET Vulkan bindings, simplifying setup for Silk.NET-based applications.

bullets.lead: FreeType font support on Nano Server
bullets.detail: Nano Server (which lacks the GDI font stack) now ships FreeType-backed font management, unblocking SkiaSharp text rendering in containerized Windows workloads.
The binding generator now produces identical output regardless of the host OS, so checked-in generated files no longer drift between Windows and Linux CI agents.

bullets.lead: CoTaskMem pixel-buffer leak in SKImage.Create raster failure path
bullets.detail: When the raster image creation path failed after allocating a CoTaskMem pixel buffer, the buffer was leaked. The failure path now correctly frees the allocation.
The `SaveTo` path now writes directly to the output stream without an intermediate buffer copy, halving allocations for large data exports.

bullets.lead: String allocation eliminated in GetEncodedText null-terminated path
bullets.detail: The null-terminated fast path in `GetEncodedText` now reuses a buffer instead of allocating an intermediate string on every call.
The uniform-name lookup map is pre-sized to the known uniform count at construction, eliminating resizes during effect setup.

bullets.lead: Windows MSVC environment initialized once per native build
bullets.detail: The MSVC toolchain environment is now set up once rather than once per target, cutting Windows native build times significantly.

bullets.lead: Containerized test targets: Azure Linux, Alpine/musl, Nano Server
bullets.detail: Three new containerized CI test legs verify SkiaSharp on Azure Linux, Alpine (musl libc), and Nano Server, expanding the supported platform matrix.
All .sln solution files are converted to the lighter .slnx format, reducing churn and improving IDE load times.
